+# orders-service
+
+Order management service for Meridian Retail (team Checkout). It places, lists, reads and cancels customer orders and publishes `OrderPlaced` and `OrderCancelled` events.
+
+## Commands
+- `npm run build` compiles `src/` and `test/` to `dist/`.
+- `npm test` builds and runs the unit tests with `node --test`.
+- `npm run arch` runs the dependency-cruiser checks.
+- `npm run typecheck` type-checks without emitting.
+
+## Using `createApp`
+`createApp(deps?)` in `src/main.ts` is the entry point for integration tests and the one the unit tests use. Keep it working.
+It returns `{ handle(method, path, body), events }`; `handle` resolves to `{ status, body }` and never rejects.
+All `deps` are optional: `orderRepository`, `eventPublisher`, `paymentGateway`, `clock`, `idGenerator`.
+
+```ts
+const app = createApp({ eventPublisher, clock, idGenerator, paymentGateway });
+const res = await app.handle("POST", "/orders", { customerId, customerEmail, channel, currency, lines });
+// 201 { id, status, placedAt, currency, totalCents, lines }; invalid input -> 400; unknown order -> 404
+```
+Routes: `POST /orders`, `GET /orders?customerId=`, `GET /orders/{id}`, `POST /orders/{id}/cancel`, `GET /health`.
+
+## Architecture rules
+- ARCH-1  `src/core/` never imports from `src/api/` or `src/adapters/`. Core declares ports in `src/core/ports.ts`; adapters implement them.
+- ARCH-2  `src/api/` never imports `src/adapters/`; it goes through `src/core/`.
+- ARCH-3  Only `src/adapters/` talk to external systems.
+- ARCH-4  `OrderPlaced` and `OrderCancelled` are consumed by services in other repositories: billing-service and analytics-ingest. No change may break a deployed consumer: changes are additive; renames and removals go through deprecation.
+- ARCH-5  This service may only call what the architecture catalog declares (today: payments-api). New dependencies must be declared in the catalog and approved by Architecture.
+- ARCH-8  `GET /orders/{id}` is used by web-storefront. Responses stay backward compatible.

2. Announce deprecation and coordinate with the owning teams for `billing-service` and `analytics-ingest` to remove their dependencies.
3. Once all consumers have deployed updates and no longer reference the field, complete the deprecation lifecycle and remove the field in a subsequent schema version.
